findings.title: Surrogate-safe truncation in sanitizeTrackingValue is unspecced - SPEC.md §5.1 rule 2 says plain 'Truncate string values to 255 characters'
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC.md §5.1 sanitization rule 2: 'Truncate string values to 255 characters.' No sentence in SPEC.md (grep confirms zero matches for 'surrogate') covers any further transformation after the truncation.
findings.evidence: app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js, sanitizeTrackingValue (diff dump lines 336-345). After `firstValue.slice(0, TRACKING_VALUE_MAX_LENGTH)`, the diff adds three lines of behavior beyond the spec text: `const lastCodeUnit = truncatedValue.charCodeAt(truncatedValue.length - 1);` and `return lastCodeUnit >= 0xd800 && lastCodeUnit <= 0xdbff ? truncatedValue.slice(0, -1) : truncatedValue;` (plus the explanatory comment line). Behavioral deviation: a value whose 255th UTF-16 code unit is a lone high surrogate is stored at 254 characters, not the specced 255. Full scope: these 3 added lines are the entire untraceable change; nothing else in the helper deviates. Provenance: fix commit fa51c91a5 ('Make tracking param truncation surrogate-safe in sanitizeTrackingParams'), resolving qa-run-2 Layer-2 finding l2-B1 (HIGH, orchestrator-reproduced: .slice(0,255) splitting a surrogate pair makes ES2019 JSON.stringify emit a lone \udXXX escape, Rails json 2.6.1 rejects the body, the entire signup POST 400s). The fix was delta-reviewed in qa-run-2 (PASS per QA-COMPLETE.md), but SPEC.md was amended only for D18/D19 - the surrogate semantics were never written into §5.1, so the code no longer traces to the spec as written, which the brief names as the Layer 1 authority. The two Jest tests fa51c91a5 added died with the deliberate utils.test.js deletion (settled baseline), leaving the behavior pinned nowhere.
findings.recommendation: Amend SPEC.md §5.1 rule 2 to record the approved behavior (e.g. 'Truncate string values to 255 UTF-16 code units; when the final kept unit is a lone high surrogate, drop it so the value JSON-serializes cleanly - 254 units in that case'), citing fa51c91a5/l2-B1. Do NOT revert the code - reverting reintroduces a reproduced HIGH (signup POST 400 on multibyte values straddling the cap). Jessica's call on the amendment wording.
